# MODIS provenance and verification limits

`ornl-documented-006.json` is the JSON example fetched from the official ORNL DAAC web-service documentation, https://modis.ornl.gov/data/modis_webservice.html, on 2026-11-15. It is NOT a fresh subset response, NOT a demo farm and NOT Collection 061: the example is MOD13Q1 Collection 006, composite A2018049, point 35.958767, -84.287433, 9×9 pixels, nominal 250 m (231.656358264 m sinusoidal grid). Raw NDVI integers use scale 0.0001, unit dimensionless; reliability is a unitless rank. Original tile, processing date and composite date are retained in every band. Attribution: ORNL DAAC, TESViS RESTful Web Service (2018), doi:10.3334/ORNLDAAC/1600; NASA MODIS/LP DAAC.

The adapter deliberately rejects this older collection rather than silently calling it 061. Its accepted Collection 061 protocol tests are explicitly synthetic and are not satellite data. Product rules were checked against https://lpdaac.usgs.gov/documents/621/MOD13_User_Guide_V61.pdf and https://www.earthdata.nasa.gov/data/catalog/lpcloud-mod13q1-061.

Live terminal requests to /products, /MOD13Q1/bands, /dates and /subset returned repeated HTTP 503 or timed out, including retries with backoff and Python/curl alternatives. Therefore no current accepted Collection 061 source-pixel fixture or end-to-end successful live subset is claimed. This is a draft integration pending recovery of ORNL; a provider outage produces an explicit unavailable response, never invented NDVI. Post-deploy: verify inventory/061 band contract, one real source pixel, three ≤10-date chunks for a full year, D1 reuse and a 375 px visual/screen-reader check. Landsat/HLS and SWIR remain unimplemented and require Earthdata access.
